jamie: FYI - we've got a spike in streaming clients in na-central dropping mid-stream. Started ~08:12 UTC. Several enterprise customers reported truncated responses and automatic reconnect loops.

support-luis: customer repro steps: open SSE to /v1/streams, send prompt, after ~10-30 tokens client receives data then connection closes with ECONNRESET. When client retries, sometimes gets 401 briefly then succeeds. Filing escalations now - some on paid dedicated instances.

simon: digging into LB and gateway logs now. Seeing many downstream TCP FINs followed by 'upstream: connection reset by peer' from the runtime. Also a handful of 401s aligned with token refresh windows.

ops-tilly: adding logs:
```
[2026-03-15T08:12:23Z] lb: conn_id=31245 idle_timeout=60 closed by lb
[2026-03-15T08:12:23Z] gateway: upstream-reset conn=31245 reason=RST
[2026-03-15T08:12:24Z] runtime: socket_write err=EPIPE pid=4412 model=redwood-13b
[2026-03-15T08:12:24Z] auth: token-refresh start user=acct-987
[2026-03-15T08:12:25Z] auth: token-refresh success user=acct-987
[2026-03-15T08:12:26Z] client: reconnect attempt=1
```

rachel: a few notes - NA-central LB idle timeout is still 60s, clients use SSE keepalive pings every 45s. If gateway doesn't forward pings properly, LB may close. Also saw worker GC spikes around same time.

jamie: Impact matrix:
- Hosted public API: degraded streaming for ~7% of requests in NA-central (frontend metrics)
- Dedicated customers: two tenants on NA-central reported partial outputs and repeated retries
- Non-streaming API (batch/generate): unaffected so far

support-luis: customers complaining about increased token usage (retries), also one billing alert for unexpected >100% token delta. Suspect retry storms.

simon: initial hypotheses: 1) LB/gateway idle timeout mismatch with SSE keepalive handling 2) token refresh race when streaming connection authenticates mid-session 3) runtime worker instability causing socket resets.

ops-tilly: immediate mitigations applied at 08:22 UTC:
- Increased LB idle timeout from 60s -> 120s in NA-central (hot config)
- Enabled explicit SSE proxying flag on gateway to pass through pings verbatim
- Temporarily routed 25% of NA-central streaming traffic to us-east to reduce pressure

jamie: @simon @rachel please confirm metrics for connection resets and HTTP 401s after the config changes.

simon: after config change: connection reset rate dropped ~60% in 10m window. 401 spikes aligned to token refresh window reduced but not resolved.

rachel: found a small bug in our token refresh middleware: when auth refresh happens mid-stream we briefly send a 401 to the client, then accept the new token - client libraries interpret that as terminal. Patch in review to avoid sending 401 during refresh (preserve connection and inject new auth header).

support-luis: repro checklist I gave to customers (works locally):
1) Open SSE to /v1/streams with expiring token (set exp in 5s)
2) Start streaming prompt, wait for token expiry and client-side refresh
3) Observe connection close within 1-3s after refresh, or partial payload received

jamie: priority actions (P0/P1):
- P0: hot patch token middleware to avoid immediate 401 during refresh (simon)
- P0: deploy LB idle timeout backfills to other AZs (ops-tilly)
- P1: add circuit-breaker / backoff guidance to SDKs to avoid retry storms (support-luis + devex)

simon: hotfix ready - small change to auth proxy to queue the new token and swap headers without returning 401. Will rollout as canary to 10% traffic in NA-central now.

deploybot: Started canary deployment 1792003478 -> 1792003485 (canary=10%)

sre-bot: Canary health: streaming success rate improved by 12% within canary, error rate down. No CPU/memory anomalies in canary workers.

jamie: rolling canary to 50% if no regressions in 5m. ops-tilly keep watch on LB metrics and backend socket resets.

ops-tilly: rolled to 50% at 08:30 UTC. Reset rate dropped further to baseline. Redirected remaining traffic to us-east back to NA-central gradually.

support-luis: customer follow-ups: two dedicated tenants confirmed streams resumed normally after ~08:33 UTC. One reported persistent truncated message — asked to collect client-side logs and request-id.

rachel: postmortem findings so far: combo of LB timeout + auth refresh race + occasional GC pause on the runtime created a window where pings weren't forwarded and token refresh produced 401 -> client libraries closed stream.

jamie: next steps (short):
- ship token middleware patch to all regions (simon)
- set LB idle timeout standard to 120s for streaming listeners (ops-tilly)
- add metric for auth-refresh-induced-401s to alerting (rachel)

longer term:
- SDK change: graceful token rotation in-client with soft retry/backoff and reattach semantics (devex)
- runtime changes: ensure GC / worker stalls don't block socket write thread (eng-runtime)

support-luis: sending status update to affected customers now (incl. mitigation steps and timeline).

jamie: thanks all. tagging incident for follow-up postmortem and action items. Please paste any collected client logs here. :heart:
